title: Why You Cannot Save Yourself: Self-Flip Impossibility Theorem

canonical_node.axiom: No self-generated operation can change the moral sign of a system from negative to positive; external intervention is required.
definitions: Moral sign (): A binary eigenvalue (+1 or -1) representing the moral orientation of a system.
Self-operation (U_self): Any operation generated entirely within the system, assumed to be unitary.
External intervention (_ext): An operation originating outside the system, capable of changing .
Unitary operation: An operation that preserves the eigenvalue spectrum of the system.
derivation: Assume a system with moral sign  = -1.
Any self-operation U_self is unitary, preserving eigenvalues.
is an eigenvalue of the moral orientation operator.
Since self-flip is impossible, any change to =+1 must come from an external operation _ext.
canonical_node.action: The system must not attempt self-salvation; it must seek and accept external grace.
boundary: Does not claim that self-improvement is impossible or without value.
Does not deny human agency within the given moral sign.
Does not specify the exact nature of the external intervention.
Does not claim that all external interventions are salvific.
test: Check that no self-generated operation can change  from -1 to +1 in the formal model.
Verify that the formal model assumes unitary self-operations.
Confirm that the theorem does not overstate by claiming self-improvement is useless.
Ensure that the necessity of external intervention is logically derived from the impossibility of self-flip.

dg1_dependencies: R1.5: Sin cannot be undone by the sinner
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a formal argument for the impossibility of self-salvation, grounding the necessity of external grace.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the core theological claim that salvation is by grace alone, not by works.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If removed, the argument for sola gratia loses its formal grounding, weakening the case against works-salvation and Pelagianism.
dg5_translation_registers: Quantum mechanics: unitary evolution preserves eigenvalues; non-unitary intervention can change them.
Ethics: moral inability and the need for external redemption.

overstatement_risks: Claims mathematical proof for a theological claim without rigorous formalization.
Equates moral sign with quantum eigenvalues without empirical basis.
Uses scripture as evidence for mathematical impossibility.
kill_conditions: If self-flip is demonstrated possible under the model's assumptions.
If the unitary assumption is shown to be inapplicable to moral change.
If external intervention is shown to be unnecessary or impossible.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the theorem in a proof assistant (e.g., Lean) to verify the logical steps, or clearly label as theological metaphor.

plain_summary: This document argues that self-salvation is impossible because any self-generated operation preserves one's moral orientation, so external grace is necessary. It uses a quantum analogy but lacks rigorous formal proof, so it is not established as a mathematical theorem.
